title: C482/580/2022 of SAURABH PAL Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
SL.
No Date
Office Notes, reports,
orders or proceedings
or directions and
Registrar's order with
Signatures
COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
23.08.2022 C482 No. 580 of 2022
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Ashish Goswami, Advocate, for
the applicants.
Mr. Siddharth Bisht, Brief Holder, for
the State.
The complainant respondent No. 2,
is present in person. The applicants have
joined the proceedings in person through
video conferencing. The applicants, who are
4 in number, are duly identified by their
learned counsel for the applicants.
In the present C-482 Application,
the applicants have prayed for quashing of
the FIR, being FIR No. 14 of 2019, registered
against them at P.S. Raipur, district
Dehradun, for their alleged involvement of
the applicants, in commission of the
offences under Sections 498A, 323, 504 of
the IPC, to be read with Section 3/4 of the
Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
Simultaneously, they have also put a
challenge to the summoning order dated
19.02.2021, which has been passed by the
Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Dehradun, where the principal proceedings
are pending consideration. The present C-482 Application is accompanied with a
Compounding Application No. IA/1/2022,
preferred under Section 320 of the Cr.PC.
duly signed by the parties to the
proceedings of the present C-482

Application, as well as their respective
counsels.
In the application thus filed under
Section 320 of the Cr.PC., the complainant
i.e. respondent No. 2 herein, submits that
owing to certain later developments, which
has taken place resulting to an execution of
a settlement deed before the Mediation
Centre, Family Court, Saket, Delhi and the
consequential decree of divorce under
Section 13B(2) of the Hindu Marriage Act,
which has been rendered on 04.04.2022,
she has settled her scores in terms of the
consenting divorce decree dated
04.04.2022, and as such, she submits that
she doesn't want to prosecute the
proceedings, which have been registered by
her by way of an FIR No. 14 of 2019, as
against the present applicants, because she
is agreeable with the terms and conditions
of the divorce decree as rendered in HMA
Case No. 245 of 2020, Saurabh Pal Vs.
Shalini Pal, by the judgment of the Principal
Judge, Family Court, South East Saket, Delhi,
which finds reference to the statement,
which has been recorded by the parties to
the proceedings before the Court, resulting
into culmination for the grant of consent
decree under Section 13B(2) of the Hindu
Marriage Act.
The learned counsel for the
applicants, while making reference to the
statement of complainant respondent No. 2,
which has been recorded before the Court
below, for the purposes of settlement of a
permanent alimony under Section 25 of the
Hindu Marriage Act, has made reference to

the statement recorded in para 3, before
the Family Court. Para 3 of the affidavit is
extracted hereunder:-
"3. We have amicably settled all our
disputes before the counseling/mediation centre
Family Court South East Saket New Delhi on
14.12.2021 the same has been already been
annexed with the petition as Annexure-A,
Pertaining to this marriage including the
maintenance (Present, Past And Future), dowry,
Permanent alimony, for the full and final
consideration amount of Rs. 8,50,000/- (Rupees
Eight Lakhs Fifty Thousand Only). It is settled that
the petitioner has paid the amount of Rs.
2,50,000/- (Rupees Two Lakh Fifty Thousand Only)
through vide D.D. no. 948221 to the petitioner no.
2 at the time of recording the statements in First
Motion on 19.01.2022."
This Court interacted with the
complainant/respondent No. 2, who had
made a categorical statement, that she has
already received a sum of Rs. 5,00,000/- out
of the total finally settled alimony of Rs.
8,50,000/-. The balance amount of Rs.
3,50,000/- is being paid to her today in the
Court, through Draft No. 948645 dated
01.07.2022, drawn in the name of
respondent No. 2 herein, from the State
Bank of India, Dehradun branch. The original
draft, is to be handed over by the Bench
Secretary of this Court to the
complainant/respondent No. 2, after
retaining the xerox copy of the same, after
taking her endorsement of receipt.
In view of the aforesaid settlement,
since the parties have already mutually
severed their matrimonial relationship
under Section 13B(2) of the Hindu Marriage
Act, in terms of the mediation settlement,

coupled with the fact that the alimony as
stated to be agreed to be accepted by
respondent No. 2, has been paid to her and
in view of the observations made above, the
present Compounding Application would
stand allowed as a consequence thereto, the
proceedings, which were drawn as a
consequence of the registration of the FIR
under Sections 498A, 323, 504 of IPC to be
read with Section 3/4 of the Dowry
Prohibition Act, 1961, which was registered
as Case Crime No. 14 of 2019, before the
learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Dehradun,
would hereby stand quashed.
Accordingly, C482 Application would
stand allowed.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 23.08.2022
Mahinder/
